COHORT_SW1.scope: Independent cohort methodology exploration; source-defined point classification, not the v1 sensor configuration or event endpoint.
limitations: Processed source CSVs lack timestamp and day identifiers; no verified chronological order, event matching, alarm/day or true time coverage claims.
Labels follow source <4 mmol/L plus duration rules and backfilled reference, unlike PhysioCGM native <70mg/dL.
Precomputed wearable feature causality is based on source code review, not full raw-data reconstruction.
No clinical or prospective efficacy conclusion; input sensors differ from PhysioCGM.
Patient-specific calibration not used; training/validation row partition is descriptive within other subjects and test subject is entirely unseen.

limitations: Processed source CSVs lack timestamp and day identifiers; no verified chronological order, event matching, alarm/day or true time coverage claims.

CONTEXT_V1_ABORTED.reason: Original 120-row purge at each side leaves 241-row separation; source IOB may span240 minutes plus reference confirmation up to15 minutes. This fails the conservative non-overlapping support audit under the nominal minute-row assumption.
CONTEXT_V1_ABORTED.action: Original process had already completed when interruption was attempted; quarantined its local outputs before effect summarization or result-driven selection. Excluded all effect claims. Replacement v1.1 uses150-row purge per side (301-row separation) and explicitly retains unverified timestamp limitation.
limitations: Even the wider purge does not establish complete source timestamp provenance.

CONTEXT_V1_1.effect_scope: Exploratory primary contextual AP contrast only; no event-alarm acceptance
limitations: Same previously viewed processed cohort; all contrasts exploratory and intervals unadjusted.
Missing complete timestamps: row support is nominal, not proven temporal or prospective validation; no alarm/day or event metrics.
Source IOB is a unitless past-injection activity index, not remaining insulin dose.
Context requires diary entries; missing fields and zeros do not establish true absence of injections or food.
Personal training and validation require earlier source-reference labels. Calibration uses the same validation segment used in model/threshold selection; no separate calibration cohort.
Point-level observed-reference opportunity fraction is not true sensor uptime; no actual device measurement-coverage claim.

ECG_CAPTURE_PILOT1.scope: Four-record signal capture pilot; no glucose or clinical alarm claim

frozen_protocol.scope: Four-record signal capture pilot; no glucose or clinical alarm claim
frozen_protocol.hr_definition: 60 / median RR seconds; retain RR in [0.3,2] for both reference and candidate; >=5 intervals
frozen_protocol.interpretation: Record choice and defaults fixed before scoring; convenience pilot, not complete MIT-BIH validation. End-of-window extraction may use any sample within the past window; no zero-latency claim. Test labels never tune detector settings.

limitations: Four convenience records only; not all48 records or an independent target-device cohort.
ECG capture validation, not PPG, glucose estimation, hypoglycemia or clinical alarm validation.
Within-window retrospective defaults may use future samples relative to an individual beat; all samples precede window-end output.
Two-second edges per five-minute window and incomplete tails unscored for both methods.
HR uses RR in0.3–2s for both methods and expert reference; does not validate abnormal intervals or HRV morphology.
No detector replacement in PhysioCGM until a separate all-record check and target-domain quality gate.
